title: One-pot synthesis of an unusual manganese–lanthanide–ferrocene cluster: A combination of d-, f-metals and an organometallic fragment

material_class.structural_family: square-in-square Mn4Nd4 core with two ferrocene-1,1'-dicarboxylate ligands

synthesis.procedure: Under aerobic conditions, to a stirred slurry of preformed [MnIII2MnII4O2(Piv)10(4-Me-py)2.5(PivH)1.5] (2) (0.20 g, 0.11 mmol) and N-butyldiethanolamine (0.18 g, 1.10 mmol) in MeCN (20 ml) was added Nd(NO3)3·6H2O (0.19 g, 0.44 mmol), then ferrocene-1,1'-dicarboxylic acid (0.015 g, 0.055 mmol). The solution was heated for 40 min at ~70 °C, filtered and concentrated by slow evaporation to give pale green–brown plate-like crystals of 3 after 7 days. The crystals were collected by filtration, washed with MeCN, and dried in air.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: stirred slurry in MeCN; aerobic one-pot reaction, then filtration and slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered, concentrated by slow evaporation; pale green–brown plate-like crystals collected by filtration, washed with MeCN, dried in air

properties.summary: DC susceptibility of 3 shows χMT = 18.33 cm3 mol−1 K at 300 K, close to 18.55 cm3 mol−1 K expected for 4 MnIII (S = 2) and 4 NdIII (4I9/2) with diamagnetic low-spin FeII. χMT decreases to 15.10 cm3 mol−1 K near 5.5 K and 13.3 cm3 mol−1 K at 1.8 K, indicating antiferromagnetic interactions plus thermal depopulation of NdIII Stark sublevels and a significant ground-state spin. Magnetization at 1.8 K rises without saturation to 16.62 μB at 5 T, implying low-lying excited states. No hysteresis and no out-of-phase AC signal above 1.8 K, so no slow relaxation/SMM behaviour in this range.
